title: Kite — From notes to next
structure:
30.0 seconds,1920×1080,30fps. Five shots in three ten-second HyperFrames compositions.

| Time | Structure and purpose |
| --- | --- |
|0–4s|New cinematic paper still life, source kite_core_paper_v1 0–4s; benefit headline over blank physical paper.|
|4–10s|Illustrative release-note attachment, same three fictional Relay facts, one message sent to Kite.|
|10–20s|Kite reply; Preview button press at12s; distinct Relay page revealed; source facts persist.|
|20–26s|Feedback asks to lead with team handoff; at23.12s draft headline changes from “A shared inbox. A clearer day.” to “Every handoff. Handled.”|
|26–30s|Kite CTA; revised draft remains on screen; ready-for-review ending, no publication claim.|

Clean cuts at4,10,20s; in-scene state swaps and sequential reveals. Original local112BPM instrumental and action accents; no narration and captions explicitly skipped because no speech. Final score fades across last1.6s; picture holds. Editable index.html and compositions/frames/ in videos/kite-core-demo/.
prompts:
Short request selected by the agent for this demo: “Make a short Kite.ai launch video showing release notes becoming a draft launch page, then improving through feedback.” This is not represented as a verbatim user quotation.

S01 exact Fal positive prompt:

A single five-second cinematic macro product still life. On the right half of a dark charcoal desk sits one small sculptural folded paper kite, matte sky blue paper, a clean simple diamond fold with a short paper tail, beside three blank warm ivory note cards. The left half is mostly empty dark negative space for titles added later. Soft large window light from camera left reveals real paper fibers and fold edges, restrained natural shadows. The objects stay perfectly still. One very slow straight camera push inward, no orbit, no cuts, no transformation, no hands or people. Premium understated product photography, tactile materials, physically coherent contact shadows. All paper and surfaces are completely blank. Landscape composition.

Negative prompt:

text, letters, logos, watermark, people, hands, object morphing, fluttering paper, fast camera, cuts, excessive blur

S02–S05 are deterministic: the exact creative instructions, copy, timelines, and geometry are in videos/kite-core-demo/STORYBOARD.md and compositions/frames/01-notes.html,02-draft.html,03-feedback.html. Their authoring directive was to preserve the same release facts, expose the Preview action and visible headline revision, and keep the result beside the CTA. Source images were not generated; the paper shot contains no people.

Audio used no model prompt: make_score.py defines original plucked D/B/G/A harmony,112BPM,seed923,48kHz stereo, soft pulse and action accents. No external samples.

routing_decisions:
General library resolved to /Users/joydimapilis/Desktop/untitled folder/Startup Launch Videos (11 accessible files). Three selected sources: Motion-5-Motion plans the video scene by scene before building it..mp4 (actual content Grok Bot), Cero.mp4, Paper.mp4. Chronological source samples and closer joins reviewed before shot planning; reference gate passed. Their principles: one request with visible consequences, color continuity into exact UI, and readable interaction holds.

Fold core lessons informed same-object story, two visible actions, no text distortion, and ending with visible work. Crumb's pre-Phase2 stationary product result supported a small Kling candidate test. Core routing had no directly compatible paper T2V success before this run; decision explicitly bounded, not forced from unrelated human-shot evidence. Exact UI routes to HyperFrames through shot_plan.py. Alternatives after weak take: simplify or regenerate within same ledger, then deterministic paper composition if needed. They were not needed. Phase2 movement library and conditioned footage excluded.
revisions:
The first paid take was selected after complete sampled chronology review; no paid regeneration. Left title room was less generous than requested, handled by readable authored overlay.

First assembled candidate rejected: hoisted video covered the headline; reused Onest subset lacked Latin glyphs and fell back to serif; headline line boxes overlapped. Corrected host/video stacking, transparent opening ground, captured Latin font, safer line-height and stable editable IDs. An intermediate font-face syntax error was caught by lint and corrected. Final composition checks: no errors/warnings,42/42 contrast checks. Before/after sources and snapshots retained in .context/kite-core-demo; composition-revisions.json records decisions. Final encoded review accepts result.
failed_attempts:
No rejected or failed paid API attempts. Exactly one new paid video-generation request.

Local first reference extraction failed because this ffmpeg lacks drawtext; reran chronological extraction without that optional filter. Installed SFX and assembler helper imports failed because a packaged media-fetch module was missing. Optional external SFX unnecessary; original score already contains action accents. Assembly dependency restored with official upstream module and a local import adapter under .context/kite-core-demo/tooling, without editing core files or global skills.

First composition failed visual/layout review and one intermediate font edit failed lint; both corrected before rendering. First reverse-engineering check on the actual rendered film failed while this document was absent; its recorded message is videos/kite-core-demo/document-gate-before.txt. The film was not marked complete at that point.
final_learnings:
Use the actual captured Latin font subset, not merely a file named Onest. Check generated-footage layering after automatic media hoisting; successful assembly does not prove headline visibility. One paper-object test can complement exact authored UI without involving human realism research. Selected take and subjective screening scores were written to the shared scorecard; refreshed core evidence now offers this single compatible result provisionally for future product T2V tests. It is not a broad best-model claim.

Production estimated API cost$0.56; shared reservation$0.65 with15% buffer; hard ceiling$10. Confirmed account billing unavailable. Original local music,UI and rendering$0 provider spend. Verification artifacts: check-03.json,encoded-review.json,and final-folder verification.json written only after actual decode/audio/preview checks and this per-video documentation gate pass.

Limits: illustrative UI, not logged-in backend capture; no audience test, independent listening, or exhaustive frame-by-frame aesthetic validation. Visual review uses full-duration chronological decoded samples and selected joins. Automated motion subcheck disabled; sampled encoded transitions and encoded-preview equivalence provide separate evidence. No narration; no speech or lip-sync claims.
